_comment: Source of truth for site/standards.html (DOC-004). status: supported | partial | planned. diagram: file in site/diagrams/ (without .svg). Keep in sync with spec/10 ticks: site/build.py fails if a ticked task's requirements cite an RFC missing here.

standards.title: Domain names — implementation and specification
standards.summary: The DNS message format and UDP/TCP transport. Parsed zero-copy; malformed packets get FORMERR or are dropped cheaply.

standards.title: Extension mechanisms for DNS (EDNS(0))
standards.summary: Bigger UDP answers, the DO bit, and options. We advertise 1232 bytes (DNS Flag Day 2020), answer unknown versions with BADVERS, and never send OPT to clients that didn't.

standards.title: DNS transport over TCP
standards.summary: Pipelined queries on one connection, answered in completion order; idle timeouts and connection caps. Upstream TCP/DoT connections are pooled and pipelined too.

standards.title: Extended DNS Errors
standards.summary: Every unusual answer says why: stale answer, blocked, not ready, no reachable upstream, overloaded.

standards.title: Minimal responses to ANY queries
standards.summary: ANY gets a tiny synthesized HINFO answer instead of everything we know, which removes an amplification vector.

standards.title: Negative caching of DNS queries
standards.summary: "No such name" answers are cached for the SOA-derived time (capped), so repeated typos and tracker probes don't hit upstreams.

standards.title: Serving stale data to improve DNS resiliency
standards.summary: If upstreams are slow or down, an expired answer (up to a day old) is served with TTL 30 and EDE 3 while the refresh continues.

standards.title: Negative caching of DNS resolution failures
standards.summary: SERVFAIL answers are cached for 5 seconds so a broken domain can't trigger a storm of retries.

standards.title: Measures for making DNS more resilient against forged answers
standards.summary: Every upstream query uses a fresh random ID and source port; answers must match ID, question, and type exactly or they're ignored.

standards.title: DNS case insensitivity clarification
standards.summary: Names are compared case-insensitively, but each client's exact letter case (0x20 randomization) is echoed back, even from cache.

standards.title: DNS over TLS (DoT)
standards.summary: Encrypted upstreams with certificate verification, SNI, and connection reuse, and a DoT listener for your devices (ALPN dot, pipelining, client IDs from the server name, certificates reloaded on renewal).

standards.title: DNS queries over HTTPS (DoH)
standards.summary: Encrypted upstreams over HTTP/2 with one multiplexed connection per server, and a DoH listener for your devices (HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1, GET and POST, client IDs in the path, Cache-Control from the answer TTL).

standards.title: DNSSEC introduction and requirements
standards.summary: Forwarded answers are validated from the root key down (with [dnssec] mode = "validate"): secure answers get AD, unsigned ones pass as they are, and bogus ones become SERVFAIL with EDE 6.

standards.title: Resource records for DNSSEC
standards.summary: DNSKEY, DS, RRSIG, NSEC, and NSEC3 are understood and checked; they're removed from answers for clients that didn't ask for them (no DO bit).

standards.title: Protocol modifications for DNSSEC
standards.summary: DO and CD toward upstreams, AD only for answers proven here and clients that asked, CD from the client returns unvalidated data, and NXDOMAIN or NODATA answers are checked against their NSEC/NSEC3 proofs.

standards.title: DNS over dedicated QUIC (DoQ)
standards.summary: QUIC transport for clients (a doq listener, UDP 853) and upstreams (quic:// URLs), one stream per query, 0-RTT off.

standards.title: Client subnet in DNS queries (ECS)
standards.summary: Strip (default), pass, or substitute per upstream. Never leaked by default — today it's always stripped.

standards.title: QNAME minimization
standards.summary: Recursive resolution that reveals only as much of the name as each server needs.

standards.title: Aggressive use of DNSSEC-validated cache
standards.summary: Answer non-existent names from validated NSEC records without asking upstream.

standards.title: DNS64
standards.summary: Synthesize AAAA records for IPv6-only clients, per group.

standards.title: Discovery of designated resolvers (DDR)
standards.summary: Let clients discover our encrypted endpoints automatically.

standards.title: Special-use domain names
standards.summary: localhost answers with loopback, .invalid and the Firefox canary get NXDOMAIN, CHAOS queries are refused, and reverse lookups for private addresses (RFC 6303) stay local unless a route covers them.
